narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile that the system weighs most heavily.

Your long tenure of over 11 years in this organization is the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward you staying. Most employees the model expects to remain have far shorter experience here, with over 85% having 10 years or less. This stability should normally signal loyalty, yet it was not enough to outweigh other signals.

The most influential factor pushing toward leaving is that you have received other job offers while working here. This stands out because the vast majority (77%) of employees predicted to stay report receiving no external opportunities. The model sees this as a clear sign you have attractive alternatives.

Your overall career experience of more than 11 years across all jobs also contributes toward predicting you will leave. While many who stay are early in their careers, your extensive background suggests you may be ready for bigger changes.

The organization should discuss your external opportunities openly with you and explore whether adjusted responsibilities, better recognition, or clearer growth paths could encourage you to stay. You may also want to reflect on whether your long service here still aligns with your current career goals.
